newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - April 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - April 4.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

A merger deal has been struck between Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd and Philippine company San Miguel Corp in a deal worth $A3.4 billion. The merger gives Coca-Cola Amatil a market value of over $A10.3 billion, with shares in the company rising 85 cents yesterday Page 1.

The Taiwan Pulp and Paper Corporation has suspended a project to build a pulp mill in Tasmania. An announcement was made yesterday to stop the second-stage of a feasibility study, because of a disagreement on the price of woodchips. The withdrawal is a major blow to Federal Government plans to attract Asian investment. Page 3.

The Australian Tax Office has announced is reviewing a range of loan structures, including split loan financing, which could become a tax audit target. A draft ruling on the legitimacy of these loans will be produced by the end of the financial year. Pag 3.

BTR Nylex managing director Philip Aiken has been appointed as BHP's executive general manager, corporate development, where he will report directly to BHP managing director John Prescott. The move is only the third time a senior post has gone outside the company. Page 39.

Colonial Mutual will be listed on the Australian Stock Exchange on May 19, with Colonial's shareholders consisting of 700,000 policy holders and the takers of a new share offer. A restriction has been placed on any one shareholder holding a maximum of 10per cent holdings in the first five years. Page 39.

Foodland Associated Ltd has announced a record interim net profit of $A28.7 million, leading to a 34 cent jump in its share price to over $A7.00. Foodland controls nearly half of the packed grocery market in Western Australia and 10.5 per cent of the retil grocery market through its Action chain. Page 42.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The Australian Stock Exchange is investigating the trading of Bank of Melbourne shares on Wednesday after Westpac Bank announced yesterday a bid of $A1.4 million for Victoria's largest regional bank. Bank of Melbourne shares increased by 65c to A$8.80 onWednesday before its stock was suspended pending the announcement. Page 21.

Coca-Cola Amatil will become the largest Coca-Cola group outside the United States following a $A3.4 billion deal with Philippine company San Miguel. Under a proposed merger of the two companies' soft drink operations, San Miguel will hold 25 percent of oca-Cola Amatil. Page 21.

Trans-Tasman group Foodland Associated Ltd has confirmed a big improvement in its New Zealand operations as stocks moved to their highest level in three years. Restructuring in operations and a share scheme has reduced issued capital by 6.95 per cent. Pae 22.

BHP has appointed former BTR Nylex managing director Philip Aiken as BHP executive general manager, corporate development. He will be largely responsible for the planning of business development and company-wide safety and environmental policies. Page 23

The grouping created by the merger of Metway Bank, Suncorp and QIDC has announced plans to cut 250 head office jobs and annual costs of $A40 million by the end of the financial year. The group expects to achieve $A115 million in profits through an improvd annual performance over the next three years. Page 23.

The Colonial Group will be listed on the Australian Stock Exchange on May 19 and expects shareholders to trade initially at more than A$1.00 above the listed price. The share float is expected to raise more than $A218 million in capital. Page 23.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Coca-Coca Amatil has proposed a $A3.4 billion merger with Philippines-based San Miguel, which would give CC Amatil 75 per cent of the growing Philippines soft drink market and a base for further Asian expansion. The market has reacted well to the move, wth CC Amatil shares rising 85c to A$12.80 yesterday. Page 25.

As part of a plan to transform the Colonial Group from a life insurer to a listed financial services group, the group will be listed on the stock exchange on May 19. This would make it one of the Stock Exchange's top 50 companies, with a $A180 million prfit expected for 1997. Page 27.

Westpac Banking Corp has announced a planned takeover of the Bank of Melbourne, only days before the release of the Wallis inquiry into the financial system. Federal Treasurer Peter Costello had asked the banks not to proceed with mergers or acquisitions efore the report was released. Page 25.

The High Court of Australia has rejected an appeal by Kerry Packer's Darling Casino to challenge the awarding of the Sydney casino licence to the Sydney Harbour Casino consortium. A deal has already been reached by Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting copany to buy the management rights to the casino from the US operator Showboat. Page 27.

Stock market analysts are predicting the sale of BHP's 37 per cent stake in Foster's Brewing in a deal worth $A1.8 billion. Sources believe the deal would see Foster's buying a 10 per cent stake in BHP with stockbroker Merril Lynch in control of the remaning shares. Page 27.

The New South Wales and New Zealand TABs are preparing to launch new services for horse racing and sports betting on the Internet. Sydney-based IWN Australasia, a subsidiary of listed high-tech company Coms21 Ltd, has signed a deal to develop an Internet etting system by the third quarter of this year. Page 28.
THE AGE

Coca-Cola Amatil has announced an aggressive expansion strategy involving plans to pay A$3.4 billion in new shares for the Coke franchise in the Philippines, despite a raging cola price war. The Australian bottler plans to take over San Miguel Corporations subsidiary Coca Cola Bottlers Philippines, in return for 293 million newly issued CCA shares. Page B1.

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has indicated it would be "concerned" on the Westpac move to take over the Bank of Melbourne, saying the bid on Victoria's only substantial regional bank would be in breach of the ACCC's 1995 gudelines onregional bank takeovers. Page B1.

The local sharemarket held firm yesterday in the face of a further Wall Street dive. Despite a 94-point drop on the Dow Jones Industrial Average, the All Ordinaries Index closed 5.8 points higher at 2361, bolstered by a strong performance from BHP, Coca Cla Amatil and Lend Lease. Page B2.

Country Road has sent a letter to major shareholder Australian Retail Investments, stating that it would not be responding to their concerns and questions. Country Road believes it has fulfilled its obligations to keep the market and shareholders informed. Page B3.

Anaconda Nickel has reached a deal with local Aboriginal groups regarding the planned $A900 million Murrin Murrin nickel-cobalt mine in Western Australia. Anaconda will pay $A1 million per year to an Aboriginal foundation, for an estimated period of 30 yars. Page B3.

Two directors have resigned from the Reef Casino Trust board as the Trust seeks to find an investor to avoid receivership. Sir Sydney Williams and John Morris resigned this week due to travel and time commitments. Page B3.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
